session_cue.text: Sir Phidipaldi slapping the Reeve with his glove

previous.text: The party reached Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map that marks places they did not recognize.
Reginald the frog warned the party that a trickster Clurichen comes from the riverbanks every night and to stay away from it.
Eric the Reeve offered a bounty to whoever kills the black dragon troubling Brandonsford. Farmer Gill says his three sons are already hunting it.
Lady Hilda offered to join a dragon hunt for pay, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would return after seeing the Reeve.
Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
Bentley said his tavern's restock shipment never arrived, and Farmer Gill said nothing has reached town in months.
Sir Phidipaldi slapped Eric the Reeve with his glove and challenged him to a duel at dawn. Bentley banished him to the Golden Egg for the night.
Dunk split from the party, and Farmer Gill told him the legend of Sir Brandon over drinks from his still.
Quinn hired Sir Phidipaldi to help get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for his vanishing ale.

current.where_you_are: Sir Phidipaldi is at the Golden Egg Tavern with its owner Quinn. Wayman and Dr. Uriah are across the street at the Clumsy Fox Tavern. Dunk is at Farmer Gill's farm on the edge of town, where Gill has welcomed him to sleep in the barn.

immediate_intention.text: Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn are setting up a fake ale shipment to catch Bentley. Quinn is to bring bottles to fill with water, and Sir Phidipaldi will make a big show of delivering them.

Your goals.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
Duel Eric the Reeve at dawn, if Sir Phidipaldi still means to press his challenge.

Standing in your way.text: Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi's false claims and glove slap, never accepted the dawn duel.

What could help.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join their dragon hunt.
If the party hires Drop Dead Ned for 100 gold a week, he and his killer wasp will do any job that lets him kill. He will refund 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the bodies.
If Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering Quinn's water-filled bottles, the fake ale shipment can bait Bentley.

Still unanswered.text: Why has nothing come into Brandonsford for months?
Who or what empties Quinn's good stock every night?

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon that tore off the woodsman George's arm may maim others who meet it.

threads.name: The unrecognized treasure map
threads.note: The party is following a treasure map whose marked locations they don't recognize; where the treasure lies is still unknown.

threads.name: The Clurichen from the riverbanks
threads.note: Reginald warned of a trickster creature that comes into town every night up to no good, a danger that stands on its own.

threads.name: The dragon and the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: Eric the Reeve offers 1000 gold for the black dragon's body, and the party gathered lore and accounts of it. The dragon remains alive and unhunted by the party.

threads.name: Lady Hilda's offer to join the dragon hunt
threads.note: Hilda would join a party for money to hunt the dragon, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would come back for her services after talking to the Reeve (beat_10).

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipments
threads.note: Bentley's restock shipment is a week overdue and nothing has come into town in months, and no one is known to have looked into why.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with Eric the Reeve
threads.note: Sir Phidipaldi insulted Eric and challenged him to a dawn duel that Eric did not accept, and Bentley sent him to the Golden Egg for the night. The ill will remains unresolved.

threads.name: Buying Shamus the mule
threads.note: Farmer Gill offered Shamus for 100 gold or for killing the dragon, and Dunk is sleeping in the barn while he considers it.

threads.name: Quinn's vanishing ale and the fake shipment
threads.note: Quinn's stock vanishes nightly and he blames Bentley. Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help stage a fake shipment for 100 gold, which has not yet happened.

facts.text: Find the treasure the party is seeking.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they don't recognize; they assume the treasure is probably at one of them.

classification.support_basis: The map narrows the treasure to a few marked places, though the party cannot yet identify them and only assumes the treasure is at one.

facts.text: Where does the treasure lie?

classification.grounding_justification: The session explicitly frames the map's locations as unrecognized and the treasure's place as only assumed to be among them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the marked places and which holds the treasure requires more than one lookup but is mainly a location fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Finding the treasure's location is useful and central to the quest but chiefly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Unfamiliar land and several marked sites naturally support asking locals and exploring to match them.

facts.text: Reginald the frog says a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away wherever it goes.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature is only said to be 'up to no good' and to be avoided; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It is described as a little trickster; nothing suggests more than mischief or minor harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on a single warning from a river frog, unconfirmed by observation.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly pattern of the creature coming into town, so the visits are ongoing.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid it, or watch for it at night, though no specific means is established.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town at night?

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald says only that it is 'up to no good', leaving its actual activity unstated; the question is suggested rather than framed.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the creature's hidden nightly activity, a hidden circumstance in town.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting; could explain local mischief but nothing established ties it to other events.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be investigated by watching the town at night or questioning locals, supporting some lead-following.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Lady Hilda would join the party's dragon hunt for pay.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armored fighter would strengthen the party against the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers hunting the dragon for money.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Hilda; benefit: an experienced armored fighter for the dragon fight.

facts.resource_subject: Lady Hilda's willingness to hunt the dragon for pay

facts.text: The woodsman George, who lives a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox, encountered the black dragon and lost an arm to it; the party could ask him where he met it.

classification.support_basis: A firsthand account could help the party find and prepare for the dragon, though George's willingness is not established.
classification.action_basis: Eric says George lives nearby and might come by tonight; he is an eyewitness, though he has not offered help.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: questioning George; benefit: where and how he met the dragon, helping the party locate it.

facts.text: Where is the black dragon, and where did it come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley notes nothing like this since Sir Brandon's dragon, and Gill says it is a different dragon and doesn't know where dragons come from.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering could reveal why a dragon appeared after centuries, beyond a simple location.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Its origin may connect to Brandonsford's dragon history, but mainly it is instrumental for the hunt.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: George, Gill and his sons are sources, and the woods can be searched.

facts.text: The black dragon outside Brandonsford, which tore off the woodsman George's arm, may maim others who encounter it.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming or killing of people who meet it is identifiable from George's injury.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: George lost an arm; serious harm to individuals.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Reported via Eric from George's account; but Gill says the dragon avoided him.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: One attack is reported and Gill's sons are hunting it now, but no ongoing pattern of attacks is shown.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon, which the bounty invites, would prevent it.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter who says she can't hunt the dragon alone, offers to join the party for money to hunt it.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned armoured fighter would add real combat strength to a party seeking to kill the dragon for the Reeve's bounty, though her fee is unset.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join a party of adventurers for money, and her fighting ability matches the need to kill the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Hilda for pay. Benefit: an experienced fighter's help in killing the dragon. Evidence: her own offer in beat_10.

facts.resource_subject: Lady Hilda's willingness to hunt the dragon for pay

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with the Reeve and come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: This was a statement of intent to return; nothing shows Hilda relies on the party coming back or would be wronged if it didn't.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill; he will refund 5 gold per kill he is allowed if he can do what he wants with the bodies.

classification.support_basis: Ned adds a willing killer and a killer wasp to a party pursuing a dragon bounty, though nothing shows he or the wasp could harm a dragon.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services for 100 gold a week, and killing is what the dragon bounty needs, a straightforward capability-to-need match.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Ned for 100 gold a week. Benefit: an extra killer with a killer wasp toward killing the dragon for the Reeve's bounty. Evidence: Ned's offer and stated killing capability (beat_21, beat_22).

facts.text: Why has nothing, including Bentley's restock shipment, come into Brandonsford for months?

classification.grounding_justification: Two independent sources say shipments have stopped: Bentley's restock is a week overdue and Gill says nothing has come in for months. Bentley calls it unprecedented since Sir Brandon's time, and the cause is never stated.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause, such as an interruption on the roads, that the town has not identified.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Bentley sets the stoppage beside the dragon rumors, so the cause could explain the town's wider troubles. That link is only suggested.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be pursued by following the supply route and questioning merchants and townsfolk.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in a duel at dawn.
facts.uncertain_reason: The challenge was one-sided and Eric never accepted; play has not shown whether Sir Phidipaldi still means to press it after being sent to the Golden Egg.

facts.text: Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi's false claims about George's dragon and the glove slap, did not accept the dawn duel, saying only that Sir Phidipaldi is more skilled at adventure.

classification.scope_basis: Eric's refusal and offense were left unresolved when Bentley separated them, and the duel was set for the following dawn, so the refusal outlasts the tavern scene.

facts.text: Buy Shamus the mule from Farmer Gill, who asks 100 gold.
Farmer Gill would accept killing the dragon outside town as work in trade for Shamus instead of 100 gold.

classification.support_basis: It offers an alternative price for Shamus if Dunk lacks 100 gold, though the dragon hunt is a large and dangerous undertaking.
classification.action_basis: Gill said, when Dunk asked about trading work, that the big work needed was killing the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: killing the dragon. Benefit: it pays Gill's price for Shamus in place of gold. This simply meets the want's own terms of sale.

facts.resource_subject: Killing the dragon as work to pay for Shamus

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night, and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn agreed to stage a fake ale shipment: Quinn brings bottles to fill with water and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering them.

classification.support_basis: With no real shipments arriving in town, a showy fake delivery of watered bottles gives the night thief bait, setting up Quinn's revenge; whether it works is untested.
classification.action_basis: Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi explicitly agreed to the plan and Quinn will supply the bottles.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: staging the fake delivery; benefit: baiting whoever steals Quinn's ale so he can get back at them; linked by the agreement in beat_36.

facts.text: Who or what empties Quinn's good stock at the Golden Egg every night?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn describes a strange nightly pattern of a full bar becoming half-empty or knocked-over glasses by morning, and only suspects Bentley without proof.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden culprit and their method behind a recurring anomaly.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain the mystery and may overturn Quinn's accusation of Bentley.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supports a stakeout, the fake-shipment bait and questioning townsfolk.
